This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of Preetham M.K. was died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26.03.2023 at about 06.30pm.

2. The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
On 26.03.2024 at about 06.30pm, the deceased was riding his friend Sagar B.L's motorcycle bearing No.KA-55-EA-6779 along with pillion rider from Bannur to Channahalli Village, between Chanahalli-Mahadevpura Bore, Mandya at that time and place the said bike skidded at the turn and rider and pillion rider both were fell down from the bike and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident the rider of the Motorcycle Preetham M K. died on the spot.

It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident deceased was hale and healthy, 23 years old, studying MA and also deceased was doing part time job in Mysore and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and contributing his earnings to his family members and leading his life happily.
Due to the sudden and untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are terribly and mentally shocked and they have lost love and affection of the deceased.

Hence, the petitioners claims Rs.15,00,000/- as the general damages for death of deceased, for mental shock and agony,
for loss of earnings, loss of future earning of the deceased, for loss of love and affections.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-55-EA-6779 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. The accident in question was taken place due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-55-EA-6779.
The Mandya District Police have registered a case against the rider of the offending Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-55-EA- 6779 in Cr.No.0055/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 338 304(A) of IPC.
For the aforesaid reasons, the claimants have prayed for awarding total compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- under various heads.
5. In pursuance of the notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement.

In spite of due service of notice the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed ex- parte.
5A.

The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement denying the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of Two Wheelers-(5 years) Bundled Policy bearing No.422800/31/2020/14849 in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 55-EA-6779 valid for Own Damage from 15.34hrs on 27.12.2019 to midnight of 26.12.2020 and liability from 15.34hrs on 27.12.2019 to midnight of 26.12.2024.

Further stated that the said motorcycle had been ridden by a person who did not possess a valid driving License and the owner knowingly allowed that person to ride the bike as on the date of accident.
Further stated that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-55-EA-6779 was owned by the 1st respondent/insured and the petitioner has suppressed the material facts and played fraud.

The deceased was not third party and he does not come within purview of terms "a person"
within Sec.147 of MV Act and deceased/rider had borrowed the insured vehicle from the owner, he had not stepped into the shoes of the owner and could not be the claimant if the accident had been caused on account of his own negligence and no additional premium is paid to cover the risk of the owner/rider.
Hence, the petition is not maintainable and same is liable to be dismissed with costs.
On the principle that a Tortfeasor cannot be the claimant and the same is contrary to law and the contract.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the age,
expenses towards funeral, income of the deceased etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant.

11. It is worth note herein that the insurer has not disputed the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.
Apart from that the Aadhaar Card, ration card produced by the petitioners are also indicates that the deceased and themselves are related to each and they are the legal heirs of the deceased.
12. It is to be noticed that the provisions contained under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, has been enunciated as a social security measure, by the Legislature.

As per amendment to motor vehicle Act, section 164 of Motor Vehicle Act reads thus:
"164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grevious hurt, etc.--(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.
(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section."
13. It provides for compensation based on the structured formula method contained in Second Schedule of the said Act.
The claimants need not prove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle for claiming compensation under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It is worth to note herein that the section 163A was the enable provision prior to amendment.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in decision reported 1(2009) 6 SCC 121, as under:
"34. . . . . . . Section 163-A of the MV Act contains a special provision as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis, as indicated in the Second Schedule to the Act.
The Second Schedule contains a table prescribing the compensation to be awarded with reference to the age and income of the deceased.
It specifies the amount of compensation to be awarded with 1 Sarla Verma - V/s - Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reference to the annual income range of Rs 3,000 to Rs 40,000.

entities.text: Sarla Verma - V/s - Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It does not specify the quantum of compensation in case the annual income of the deceased is more than Rs 40,000.
But it provides the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
The table starts with a multiplier of 15, goes up to 18, and then steadily comes down to 5.
It also provides the standard deduction as one-third on account of personal living expenses of the deceased.

Therefore, where the application is under Section 163-A of the Act, it is possible to calculate the compensation on the structured formula basis, even where the compensation is not specified with reference to the annual income of the deceased, or is more than Rs 40,000, by applying the formula: (2/3  AI  M), that is two thirds of the annual income multiplied by the multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased would be the compensation.
Several principles of tortuous liability are excluded when the claim is under Section 163-A of the MV Act."

15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 2 (2013) 9 SCC 65 has held as under:
"The 1988 Act gives choice to the claimants to seek compensation on structured formula basis as provided in Section 163-A or make an application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of Section 165 under Section 166.
The claimants have to elect one of the two remedies provided in Section 163A and Section 166.
The remedy provided in Section 163-A is not a remedy in addition to the remedy provided in Section 166 but it provides for an alternative course to Section 166.

By incorporating Section 163-A in the 1988 Act, the Parliament has provided the remedy for payment of compensation notwithstanding anything contained in the 1988 Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, that the owner of a motor vehicle or 2 Reshma Kumari & Ors -Vs- Madan Mohan & Anr authorized insurer shall be liable to pay compensation on structured formula basis as indicated in the Second Schedule in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle.

The peculiar feature of Section 163-A is that for a claim made there under, the claimants are not required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner or owners of the vehicle concerned.

The scheme of Section 163-A is a departure from the general principle of law of tort that the liability of the owner of the vehicle to compensate the victim or his heirs in a motor accident arises only on the proof of negligence on the part of the driver.

Section 163-A has done away with the requirement of the proof of negligence on the K Mahadeva Alias Mahadevaiah vs Sagar B.L on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46619595/
6 part of the driver of the vehicle where the victim of an accident or his dependants elect to apply for compensation under Section 163- A.

16. Our Hon'ble High Court in the case reported in 32007 SCC ONLINE KAR 538=ILR 2008 KAR 1249 has held as follows:
"MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTION 163-A Petition under - Award - Accident occurred due to the negligence of the victim himself - Maintainability of petition under Section 163A - HELD, A petition under Section 163A of the act is maintainable even in case where negligence is on the part of the victim - FURTHER HELD,
Even 'Obiter Dicta' made in the decision of the Supreme Court is binding on the High Court."

17. Further, Our Hon'ble High Court held in a decision reported in 42008 SCC Online Kar 19=ILR 2008 KAR 959 as follows:

Salma and Others 4 National Insurance Company Limited -Vs- Honnappa and others "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - SECTION 163(1) - Claim petition - Maintainability of - Involvement of two motor vehicles - Accident - Injuries sustained by the claimant - Grievance of the Insurance Company - Claimant, himself being the cause for the accident, whether can maintain the petition under Section 163- A of the Act - Award of compensation - Challenge to - HELD,
When two motor vehicles were involved in the accident due to which claimant sustained injuries, in such a situation, the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Act is permissible, no matter, the driver or the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident, may 11 M.V.C. NO. 215/2017 dispute his negligence in the matter -

Hence,
the tribunal has not committed any error in entertaining the petition under Section 163-A of the Act - ON FACTS, FURTHER HELD, As the entitlement of the Petitioner has been considered and awarded on structured formula basis in terms of Schedule-II of the Act, the appeal filed by the Petitioner is devoid of merits and the same is dismissed."

18. Further, our Hon'ble High Court in the case of 5Smt. M. Malini and another -Vs - ICICI Lombard Motor Insurance and others has held as follows:

Further, our Hon'ble High Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited - V/s - Smt. Rajamma and Others (M.F.A. No. 10292/2012 dated 11-11-2016) has categorically held in paragraph 14 of the said Order that when two motor vehicles are involved in the accident,
irrespective of the negligence or default of the owner/driver of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person, claim under Section 163-A is maintainable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, our Hon'ble High Court has been pleased to follow the earlier Division Bench judgment in Appaji's case (2004 ACJ 1289) to hold that non-impleadment of the owner or driver of the vehicle involved in the accident is not fatal to claim compensation under Section 163-A of the Act.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held in a decision reported (2019) 12 SCC 398 has held "the grant of compensation under section 163-A on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of a final award 6 United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Sunil Kumar and another and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle(s) involved in the accident-

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Sunil Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, though section 163-A does not specifically exclude a possible defense of the insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated by section 140(4), to permit such defense to be introduced by the insurer and/or to understand the provision of Sec.163-A to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163-A, namely final compensation within a limited time-frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situations where the claims of the compensation on the basis of fault liability were taking an unduly long time-

Further, to understand section 163-A to permit the insurer to raise the defense of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under section 163-A on a par with proceedings under section 166 which would not only be self contradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention-

Thus, in a proceeding under section 163-A of the Act, it is not open for the insurer to raise any defense of negligence on the part of the victim"
21.

Thus, in view of the above principles, I am of the humble opinion that this Court cannot go into the question of determining the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, when the petition is filed under Section 163-A or 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Thus, the contentions on behalf of the Respondents that the present petition is not maintainable, since the death of the deceased had occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased himself in riding the bike in rash and negligent manner is liable to be rejected.
Accordingly, I answer does not arise for consideration.

23.
In respect to liability is concerned, the insurer has specifically pleaded that they are not liable to pay the compensation as the policy is bundled policy.

It is necessary to elaborate the features of the bundled policy: "A bundled bike insurance policy combines both own damage (OD) and third-party (TP) coverage into a single plan, typically offering a one-year OD policy and a multi- year TP policy (e.g., 3 or 5 years) for new two- wheelers.
This means you pay for your own damage coverage annually, while the third-party coverage is secured for a longer duration.
This approach simplifies the insurance process for new bike owners, offering a convenient way to secure comprehensive coverage while managing costs.

24. The insurance policy marked at Ex.R2 depicts that the owner of the bike has insured the vehicle for OD from 27.12.2019 to 26.12.2020 and CPA sum assured Rs.15,00,000/- from 27.12.2019 to 26.12.2020 only.

The owner has paid an amount of Rs.5453/- towards basic third party liablity,
Rs.360/- towards Compulsory PA cover (Owner Driver).
As per the policy, compulsory PA cover is covered only for one year.
The accident was occurred on 26.03.2023.
It means fourth year of the policy.
The insurance policy itself clearly demonstrated that the third party liabilty for five years.
The deceased himself was the rider at the time of accident.
The entire policy does not depicts that the policy would act as ACT POLICY for next four years.
But terms and conditions and nature of the policy has clearly depicts that, rider and pillion rider would cover for first year of policy only.

Hence,
it is appears to Court that, rider of the offending bike has not termed as third party in this policy.
Therefore, I declined to fasten the liability on insurance company.
So, I answered issue No.3 partly in affirmative 25.
Issue No.4:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimants under section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part against the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/-
(Rupees Five Lakhs Only) to the claimants and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment, after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation The petitioners 1 to 4 are equally entitled for the above referred compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the entire share amount of the petitioner Nos.1 to 4 shall be released in their respective names on proper identification through e- payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The deceased was not third party and he does not come within purview of terms "a person"
within Sec.147 of MV Act and deceased/rider had borrowed the insured vehicle from the owner, he had not stepped into the shoes of the owner and could not be the claimant if the accident had been caused on account of his own negligence and no additional premium is paid to cover the risk of the owner/rider.
Hence, the petition is not maintainable and same is liable to be dismissed with costs.
On the principle that a Tortfeasor cannot be the claimant and the same is contrary to law and the contract.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As per amendment to motor vehicle Act, section 164 of Motor Vehicle Act reads thus:
"164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grevious hurt, etc.--(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.
(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section."
The claimants need not prove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle for claiming compensation under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

irrespective of the negligence or default of the owner/driver of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person, claim under Section 163-A is maintainable.
Thus, in a proceeding under section 163-A of the Act, it is not open for the insurer to raise any defense of negligence on the part of the victim"
